_note:
Re-derived 2026-09-01 after eminence-v3 merged as v1.0.2. The merge traded two artifact rocks for five mana CREATURES (Birds, Delighted Halfling, Ignoble Hierarch, and the two colour-scaling elders, which are 3-5 mana each in a five-colour deck), three counterspells for Lightning Greaves, and two dragons for four. NOTE WHAT THE PROTECTION SWAP CHANGED rather than only that it happened: Greaves answers targeted removal and cannot answer a board wipe, which the three counterspells could. The group still reads 'protection held for the big turn' and that is the turn Greaves is for, but its coverage is narrower than the count suggests.

Re-derived 2026-08-24 against the v1.0.0 paper list, because the deck's ONLY checker-verified win line left the 99. Aggravated Assault is gone, and with it stack 003 (Ventmaw + Assault infinite combats) and stack 006's driver; Savage Ventmaw and Blasphemous Act went too, so stack 004 also describes a board this deck can no longer make. THE INFINITE COMBAT LOOP target is DELETED rather than repaired: both halves are out of the maindeck, it measured 0% by construction, and a target naming cards that can never be drawn is worse than no target — it reports a rate for a plan the deck does not have.

THIS DECK NOW HAS NO VERIFIED WIN LINE, and that is the single most important fact about it. The two kill targets below are declared UNVERIFIED in their own labels, because this file is a declaration and declaring is not proving — the repo's rule is that a line is fact only once a stack carries checker.verdict == 'pass'. They are declared anyway rather than omitted, because a primary win line with NO target at all is the documented defect that let this very deck go unmeasured before: the simulator never measured how it actually wins. Two kills are declared rather than one because the deck genuinely has two and the schema cannot express their UNION — do not add their rates together.

What changed and why: Dragonlord's Servant joins the cost reducers (it is literally 'Dragon spells you cast cost {1} less', the same job as Urza's Incubator and Dragonspeaker Shaman). 'Payoff + a castable dragon' loses Savage Ventmaw, Rivaz of the Claw and Tiamat, which all left, and gains the arriving Dragons that do that job — Glorybringer, Smaug the Magnificent, Rapacious Dragon, Moltensteel Dragon. A DRAGON-RESTRICTED MANA group is new: Desolation of Smaug and Sarkhan, Fireblood both add mana spendable only on Dragon spells, which `manabase.land_colors` counts as ZERO sources by the deck-builder's rule — correct for colour maths and exactly wrong for the question 'can I cast my commander', so it is measured separately rather than folded into ramp.

model_treasures and model_combat are BOTH ON as of this revision, and turning them on is what exposed how badly the deck was being mismeasured: the commander went from 'cast by turn 6 in 0.0% of games' to 4.1%, and games where it NEVER arrives fell from 9,175 to 7,170 in 10,000. A fifth of this deck's games were being scored as 'commander never lands' because the model could not see a Treasure. Mean available mana is UNCHANGED at every turn (4.219 at t5, both ways), which is the mechanism stated exactly: a Treasure is a one-shot stockpile spent only when lands and rocks fall short, so it does not raise your average mana, it buys the one expensive turn. The Treasure group below names ALL SEVEN sources, not the two the model can spend — because the group's question is 'do I have Treasure', which is answerable for a card the model cannot read, and scoping it to the modellable two dropped Old Gnawbone out of every component while it sits in three checker-passed stacks (validate-goldfish-targets caught exactly that). Only Rapacious Dragon's ETB and Smaug's upkeep trigger actually feed the mana model; Atsushi, Cavern-Hoard Dragon, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone and Smothering Tithe are real Treasure the model cannot count, so every Treasure-derived MANA figure is a FLOOR even though this group's drawn-rate is complete. Same for combat: Ancient Gold Dragon, Atarka World Render, Hellkite Tyrant, Klauth and Thrakkus have effects the model cannot read.

CORRECTED the same day it was written, by deck-doctor and engine-critic independently. THE ENTRY KILL's payoff leg was authored with SEVEN cards and was wrong twice over. (1) Miirym and Lathliss sat in BOTH of its `any_of` groups, so `_target_met` scored one drawn card as satisfying both needs and the target could read 'assembled' off a single card. (2) Neither is a damage payoff at all — both are token MAKERS ('create a token that's a copy of it' / 'create a 5/5 red Dragon token'), and they belong in the multi-Dragon group where they now sit alone. Temur Ascendancy went too: it draws, it does not damage. And Garruk's Uprising matched a naive 'damage' text scan only through TRAMPLE REMINDER TEXT ('can deal excess combat damage'), which is the reminder-text trap this repo has documented before. The leg is now the three cards that actually convert a Dragon entering into damage: Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas. The broader 'Dragon payoff drawn (per-dragon trigger engine)' group KEEPS all seven, because its question is 'does a Dragon entering do anything', which is true of a draw trigger too.

SHARED-LEG CORRECTION, same day and same mechanism as THE ENTRY KILL's, found by this deck's own deck-engineer on a fleet scan. Thrakkus the Butcher sat in BOTH legs of THE COMBAT KILL, so one drawn card satisfied both needs. Removed from the castable-Dragon leg and kept as a combat multiplier, where it is one of four rather than one of seven. Measured: assembled 0.411 -> 0.353, by turn six 0.290 -> 0.232, mean turn 4.25 -> 4.77. The combat kill is therefore much closer to the entry kill than it looked, which strengthens rather than weakens the reading that the entry kill is the plan with evidence behind it.

THIRD CORRECTION to this file the same day, found by deck-skeptic and the third defect in a declaration the orchestrator hand-authored. THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg held FOUR cards and two of them do not multiply: Radiant Destiny is an ADDITIVE anthem (+1/+1 to a chosen type), and Garruk's Uprising grants trample and draws a card — it is the SAME card the entry kill's damage leg had to eject, matched both times by its trample reminder text ('can deal excess combat damage'). Two text scans, two false positives, one card. The leg is now the two cards that genuinely multiply Dragon combat damage: Atarka, World Render (double strike on every attacking Dragon) and Thrakkus the Butcher (doubles the power of each Dragon). This is a two-card leg and its thinness is the finding, not a defect in the measurement.

DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, raised by deck-skeptic and judged rather than reflexively 'fixed': the 'Payoff + a castable dragon by mid-game' target keeps Miirym and Temur Ascendancy in its payoff leg. That is NOT the defect corrected above. Its label says PAYOFF, not DAMAGE payoff, and a token copy or a card drawn is a real payoff for a Dragon entering — the same reason the seven-card 'Dragon payoff drawn (per-dragon trigger engine)' group keeps all seven. The two corrected legs were mislabelled specifically as DAMAGE. There is also no shared-leg violation here: Miirym sits in need[0] and Lathliss in need[1], and they do not cross. Changing membership would move a rate for no gain in truth, which is the failure mode a validator that fires on correct data teaches.

OPEN, DELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON: engine-critic's terminal round found that THE COMBAT KILL's two-card multiplier leg arguably omits SCOURGE OF THE THRONE, whose additional combat phase doubles the turn's Dragon combat damage — and the engine model itself calls it that kill's mechanism, which is an internal contradiction worth settling. It differs from Atarka and Thrakkus in being CONDITIONAL (it must attack the player with the most life), which is why it is a judgement rather than an obvious omission. It is left unchanged because the finding arrived in a TERMINAL round: this declaration has already moved three times today and every move cascaded into two artifacts, and a fourth change made after the last adversary has finished is unreviewed by construction. Settle it on the next pass, with a critic attached.
_required_note: `required` marks the components this deck cannot function without; `route` marks alternative ways to close, which are counted as a UNION rather than multiplied together. Both are JUDGEMENTS about what the deck needs — the measurement is `manamap pilot diagnose`, and it reports an ABSENT engine figure rather than a zero when nothing here is marked.
